title: Transcriptome Profile and Analysis of the Maternal-Effect Genes Related to Embryonic Axis Specialization in Eggs of the Brown Planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens (Hemiptera: Delphacidae)
content: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens (Stål) (Hemiptera: Delphacidae), is a destructive rice pest. Although maternal-effect genes were first discovered in Drosophila melanogaster, their identities and functions in most insects remain poorly understood. We performed de novo transcriptome sequencing of four cDNA libraries from short-winged female adults and their unfertilized eggs of N. lugens (two biological replicates each). A total of 86,289 unigenes were assembled (N50, 1,982 bp). Of these, 21,345 were expressed in females and 20,847 in unfertilized eggs, so 97.67% mRNAs in female adult could be passed into its eggs. Total 28 maternal effect genes related to embryonic axis specialization were identified. Compared to D. melanogaster, in N. lugens only staufen was assigned to the anterior subgroup, whereas 9, 4, and 14 genes were assigned to posterior, terminal, and dorsal–ventral subgroups, respectively. Ten randomly selected DEGs were validated by qRT-PCR, with trends generally consistent with RNA-seq. These results provide a transcriptome-level resource and candidate gene set for understanding maternal regulation of embryonic axis specialization in N. lugens and for future CRISPR- or RNAi-based functional studies.
